learning_outcomes.text: Acquire basic knowledge and concepts of Numerical Analysis, with main focus on applications.
Be able to implement numerical algorithms in order to solve practical problems.
Become familiar and be able to work with various numerical algorithms and models.
Gain the ability to apply numerical algorithms to solve practical and real-life problems.
Ability to use approximation and numerical features of various mathematical software.
Use of computer science and mathematical models and tools for solving specific problems in the application field.
Defining basic concepts, theory and mathematical models.
Identifying the appropriate models and methods for solving real-life problems.
Embedding formal models in applications from various areas.

Ability to conform to the requirements of organized and efficient work, to develop a responsible approach towards the academic and scientific fields, in order to make the most of one’s own creative potential, while obeying the rules and principles of professional ethic.

Using efficient methods and techniques for learning, information, research and developing capabilities for using knowledge, for adapting to a dynamic society and for communicating in Romanian and in a worldwide spoken language.

syllabus_topics: Preliminaries. Taylor polynomials. Errors, sources, propagation. Stability and conditioning of a problem. Divided and finite differences.
Solution of systems of linear algebraic equations. Direct methods. Gaussian elimination. Backward and forward substitution. Factorization (LU, LUP, QR, Cholesky) methods. Examples.
Iterative methods. Jacobi and Gauss-Seidel methods. SOR method. Conditioning of a linear system. Ill-conditioned matrices.
Approximation of functions. Polynomial interpolation. Lagrange interpolation, Lagrange fundamental polynomials. Error in Lagrange interpolation. Optimal choice of nodes. Examples.
Efficient computation of interpolation polynomials. Barycentric formula. Newton’s divided and finite differences interpolation. Aitken’s algorithm. Examples.
Hermite interpolation. Interpolation with double nodes. General case. Error in Hermite interpolation. Special cases.
Birkhoff interpolation. Birkhoff fundamental polynomials. Peano’s theorem and the error in Birkhoff interpolation. Examples.
Spline interpolation. Linear and cubic splines. Properties. Least squares approximation. Orthogonal polynomials.

Numerical differentiation and integration. Numerical differentiation formulas. Examples. Interpolatory and Newton-Cotes quadratures. Composite rectangle, trapezoidal and Simpson’s rules. Examples. Adaptive quadratures.
Richardson extrapolation. Iterated quadratures. Romberg’s method. Gaussian quadratures. Families of orthogonal polynomials. Examples.

Rootfinding for nonlinear equations. Iterative methods. Order of convergence. Bisection, secant and Newton’s methods. Comparison between Newton’s and secant methods. Aitken extrapolation. One-point iteration methods, successive approximations. Examples.
Newton’s method for multiple roots. Newton’s method for nonlinear systems. Examples.
Review of Matlab.
Taylor polynomials. Errors.
Newton’s divided and finite differences.
Linear algebraic systems I. Gaussian elimination. Factorizations. Backward and forward substitution.
Linear algebraic systems II. Iterative methods. Jacobi, Gauss-Seidel, SOR methods.
Lagrange interpolation I. Lagrange fundamental polynomials. Barycentric formula.
Lagrange interpolation II. Newton’s form. Aitken’s algorithm.
Hermite interpolation with double nodes. Summary and review of polynomial interpolation.
Cubic spline interpolation. Least squares approximation.
Numerical Integration I. Newton-Cotes quadratures. Adaptive quadratures.
Numerical Integration II. Romberg’s method. Gaussian quadratures.
Numerical methods for nonlinear equations.

assessment_methods.method: Participation in discussing and solving problems throughout the semester

assessment_rules: A grade of 5 or above (on a scale from 1 to 10) is required on each of the activities: written exam and lab evaluation.
